title: Frequency-Multiplexed Parallel Gates for Quantum LDPC Codes in a Two-Dimensional Ion Crystal
authors: G. -X. Tang, L. -M. Duan, Y. -K. Wu
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes admit high encoding rates but require nonlocal entangling gates for syndrome measurement. Instead of physically moving the qubits which slows down with the increasing qubit number, here we propose to achieve parallel nonlocal entangling gates on a two-dimensional (2D) ion crystal using frequency-multiplexing. Adiabatic conditions ensure the suppression of gate infidelity and crosstalk error, as well as their robustness against slow drift in the trap frequency which is a leading error source in ion trap. We consider a numerical example of a $[[248,10,18]]$ bivariate bicycle code on a 2D crystal of 512 ions. By optimizing the mapping of the qubits and the assignment of the frequency bands for multiplexing, we show that a moderate laser power is sufficient for parallelism, and that a logical error rate of $10^{-12}$ can be achieved under realistic noise parameters.
summary: This paper proposes using frequency-multiplexing on a 2D ion crystal to implement parallel, high-fidelity entangling gates necessary for quantum error correction using qLDPC codes. By designing adiabatic pulses, the scheme suppresses common errors like crosstalk and trap frequency drift. The results show that this approach can achieve a target logical error rate of $10^{-12}$ using moderate laser power, advancing the feasibility of large-scale quantum computation in ion traps.
main_problem: The core challenge is implementing scalable, parallel nonlocal entangling gates required for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes without relying on slow and error-prone physical qubit shuttling.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that a frequency-multiplexing scheme on a 2D ion crystal can achieve a logical error rate of $10^{-12}$ for a specific qLDPC code using moderate laser power.
method: The method combines frequency-multiplexing to enable parallel gates with adiabatic pulse design to suppress gate infidelity and crosstalk errors.
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-dimensional (2D) ion crystal hosting qubits. The theoretical model involves designing entangling gates using an effective Hamiltonian and analyzing error sources like crosstalk and trap frequency drift.
key_observables: Logical error rate ($p_L$), gate fidelity ($\delta_F$), and crosstalk error ($\epsilon_c$).
important_parameters: The system is analyzed using a $[[248, 10, 18]]$ bivariate bicycle code on 512 ions, with gate time $T=1$ ms.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA) for crosstalk estimation and assumes specific noise models for error rate extrapolation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the frequency-multiplexed gate scheme, performance metrics showing error scaling with detuning and drift, and the final logical error rate vs. Rabi rate trade-off.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for parallel gates, detailing the frequency-multiplexing technique and its robustness, to simulating the full QEC circuit performance and estimating the final logical error rate.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the scaling bottleneck in trapped-ion quantum computing by proposing a hardware-efficient method (frequency multiplexing) to implement complex quantum error correction circuits.
